gap_notes: CORE cannot be scored yet: ingested sources are still classical only (Ptolemy, Lilly, Valens). Psychological, living-traditional, and professional schools pending.

Valens I.1 is a topical/significator catalog (sect, colour, taste, body parts), not Ptolemy/Lilly elemental qualities. Do not backfill heat/cold/dry/moist from Valens, and do not average catalogs into function.
Valens I.1 is childbearing, gifts, offices, release from bonds; day sect. It does not attest Ptolemy/Lilly temperate hot-moist.
Corpus has no dedicated psychological title for Jupiter. Do not invent a Greene-Jupiter locus.
Object-level themes mix compared and school_specific lemmas. Per-lemma evidence_tier stays in this ledger; knowledge-object schema is not expanded for that.
Layer 1 requires positive_expression; it is filled from Lilly well-dignified manners only until a second school class is compared. Valens is still source_class=classical.

claims.author: Claudius Ptolemy / J.M. Ashmand trans.
claims.locus: Tetrabiblos Book I Chapter IV (Ashmand p.14)
claims.original_claim: Jupiter lies between Saturn's cold and Mars's heat and therefore has a temperate influence, promoting warmth and moisture.
claims.normalized_claim: Jupiter is temperate, warming and moistening

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter IX Nature (1659 p.61–62)
claims.original_claim: Jupiter is a diurnal masculine planet, temperately hot and moist, airy, sanguine.

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter IX Manners when well placed (1659 p.61–62)
claims.original_claim: When well placed: magnanimous, faithful, fair-dealing, charitable, liberal, just, prudent, indulgent to wife and children.
claims.normalized_claim: Dignified Jupiter: magnanimous, just, liberal, fair-dealing

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter IX When ill (1659 p.62)
claims.original_claim: When ill: wastes patrimony, hypocritically religious, tenacious of false tenets, careless of friends, crouching without necessity.
claims.normalized_claim: Debilitated Jupiter: waste, hypocrisy, dull excess of yielding

claims.author: William Lilly
claims.locus: Book I Chapter IX Colour and Motion (1659 p.61)
claims.original_claim: Jupiter finishes the zodiac in twelve years; faster than Saturn, slower than Mars.

claims.author: Vettius Valens / Mark Riley trans.
claims.edition: Riley unperfected English; Kroll 1908 / Pingree 1986 Greek
claims.locus: Anthologies Book I ch.1 Nature of the Stars
claims.original_claim: Jupiter indicates childbearing, political ties, gifts, offices, justice, inheritance, and relief from troubles; it is of the day sect.
claims.normalized_claim: Valens' Jupiter is gifts, office, and release, not an elemental temperate package
